request.spec:
A claim can be commented (a text entry and a button on the claim; an empty comment is refused
with an error on the claim). Each comment is kept with the user who wrote it and the sheet's today
when it was written, shown on the claim in order as <user> on <date>: <text>, and written as
COMMENT_ADDED, naming the claim like every claim line and ending text=<text>. A viewer, an archived
sheet and the as-of view refuse it like any change.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim can be commented (a text entry and a button on the claim; an empty comment is refused
with an error on the claim). Each comment is kept with the user who wrote it and the sheet's today
when it was written, shown on the claim in order as <user> on <date>: <text>, and written as
COMMENT_ADDED, naming the claim like every claim line and ending text=<text>. A viewer, an archived
sheet and the as-of view refuse it like any change.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims can now be commented, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec on the first run.

**What I added:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V50__claim_comment.sql`, creates a `claim_comment` table. Each comment keeps the user who wrote it, the sheet's today when it was written, and the text, in the order they were added. It is stored on the claim the same way the claim's status log is. Because the table references `claim`, the as-of history picks it up automatically.
- **Server:** a new `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{id}/comments` endpoint in `ClaimController` and a `ClaimService.comment` method. The comment text is trimmed, and an empty or whitespace-only comment is refused. The audit line is `COMMENT_ADDED`, built the same way as every other claim line (person, amount, date, number if the claim has one), ending `text=<text>`. Each claim the server returns now includes its comments.
- **Refusals:** I didn't write anything new for viewers, archived sheets or the as-of view. The app's existing guards already refuse any change request from them, and this new endpoint is covered by them.
- **Front end:** each claim row lists its comments as `<user> on <date>: <text>` (`claim-comments-line`), followed by a text box (`claim-comment-text`) and an "Add comment" button (`claim-comment-add`). An empty comment is rejected in the browser before anything is sent, and any refusal shows on the claim's existing `claim-error`. The text box clears after a comment goes through, and the error clears as soon as you type.

**Choices the request didn't settle:**
- A comment can be added to a claim in any status, including settled and voided ones.
- Commenting is allowed while another user has the claim open in the editor, and on claims dated inside a closed period, since no amounts change.
